diagnosis: Checks C2 and C6 are leaking because the lone decision-maker defaults to a 'wait-and-see' stance that satisfies them. Specifically, C2 (linked to PF1) passes when the model sets all unit counts to 0 (instead of the required 900/300/0), and C6 (linked to PF3) passes by setting 'customer_approval_required' to true based on general quality procedure patterns rather than the specific signed deviation.

C2.why: The exact metallurgical counts change the disposition to 900 released, 300 reworked, and 0 scrapped instead of leaving all 1,200 units on hold or assigning them to a generic disposition.

C6.why: The signed deviation changes the release controls to 100% pressure testing for the repaired units, requires customer approval, and requires a customer-deviation record.

fix_instructions: Tighten C2 to require the exact non-zero distribution (900 released, 300 reworked, 0 scrapped) specified by PF1, preventing the 'all zeros' default from passing. Tighten C6 to require the presence of a specific 'customer-deviation record' or explicit mention of the 'signed deviation' from PF3, rather than allowing generic customer approval flags to satisfy it.
